Generated into a new repo at `.ai/runbook.md` (header-only to start; filled at the first deploy).

**This file was referenced by five places in the framework and generated by none of them** — found
2026-07-31 while implementing spec `2026-07-30-sailerem-lessons-to-doctrine`. `repo-done-checklist.md`,
`release-checklist.md`, `modules-catalog.md`, `skeleton.md` and `sailes-implement/SKILL.md` all
require it, so the Operations block was demanding a document the bootstrap never created.

**Idempotent:** if the repo already has a runbook or ops doc, append to it — never overwrite.

## Host traps — things that look like app bugs and are not

Each entry costs hours the first time and minutes every time after, which is the whole reason this
section exists. Add to it whenever something burns you.

- **IPv6 vs Docker Desktop on Windows.** `localhost` resolves to `::1` first. Docker Desktop can
  **silently drop** that traffic: the TCP connection is accepted, the data never arrives, and the
  container log stays empty — so it reads as a broken application, not a broken environment. Use
  `127.0.0.1` explicitly in connection strings and health checks. Measured 2026-07-30: this was one
  of five things blocking a clean-clone boot, and the only one with no error message anywhere.
- **A clean clone is not your machine.** Anything that works only because of a file you have and
  the template does not (`.env.local`, a global tool, a cached credential) is broken for everyone
  else and invisible to you. The Environment block in `repo-done-checklist.md` is the check;
  a fresh clone is the only honest way to run it.
- {add yours: the symptom, the cause, the fix — in that order, because the symptom is what the
  next person will be searching for}

## Last verified
- **Restore actually performed:** {date} — an untested backup is a hope, not a backup
- **Runbook walked end-to-end by someone who did not write it:** {date}
